Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

hi! I built a small opencode TUI plugin: /context shows exactly how the built-in Context panel number is composed — input (no cache), output, reasoning, cache read/write, cache hit rate and cost — plus the session-wide total. When you delegate with task, it walks the child sessions and adds a Subagents block and a combined total (subagent usage is excluded from the parent's panel).
Zero runtime dependencies, never calls an LLM, exact numbers (no estimates). Install with opencode plugin opencode-context-usage (restart after). Repo: https://github.com/angeloper86/opencode-context-usage — feedback and issues welcome!
It is sad to see this PR being closed...

This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #48372: Same `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')` crash at `SystemPrompt.environment` in a compiled Bun build, reproducing on version 1.18.30 with identical stack trace.

The compiled Bun 1.4.2 reproduction in #48397 identifies the filesystem/search runtime cycle as the cause of this `SystemPrompt.environment` `a.name` failure. Its regression covers an authenticated session, a real `read` tool call, completion and a second turn; the fixed build passes with three deterministic local-provider requests.

Closing this issue as a duplicate of #48372, which reports the same compiled Bun `SystemPrompt.environment` `a.name` failure. #48397 contains the narrower filesystem/search cycle diagnosis and regression fix.

I traced the current v2 path before suggesting an implementation boundary. `SessionProcessor.create()` captures before `llm.stream()`, and `step-finish` captures again; each `Snapshot.track()` scans changed/untracked paths and runs `write-tree`, even when the attempt never mutates files. The stream event is also too late for ownership: the AI SDK can execute a tool before `step-start`. The earlier usable boundary is the `SessionTools.resolve()` execute wrapper, before `tool.execute.before` and the tool implementation.

I suggest a bounded first slice:

- Scope one epoch to one mutating tool invocation, not a whole message/turn. Serialize mutating invocations by worktree initially; read-only tools remain concurrent.
- Classify built-ins as read-only, exact-path (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`), or opaque (`shell`, code execution, plugin tools). Exact paths come from validated input; opaque tools use a conservative whole-worktree pre/post capture.
- Persist an `open` epoch keyed by worktree plus session/message/call provenance before any plugin hook or tool side effect. Settlement records postimage, owned paths, and expected current state. A process restart leaves an explicit reconciliation record rather than attributing whatever is currently on disk.
- Make revert write-ahead: persist the restore plan and expected-current hashes before touching files. A mismatch becomes a conflict in this first slice—no silent overwrite or force fallback—then completion/clear is persisted after the worktree operation.
- Keep retention/shared-object-store policy and “undo message only” outside this first slice. Preserve the scoped-restore behavior from #45141 while the epoch model is introduced.

I would verify behavior with integration tests that assert: model-only/retry/read-only paths invoke no snapshot Git work; the durable preimage happens before a mutating side effect; concurrent sessions serialize worktree mutations; an external edit causes a conflict instead of being overwritten; and crashes before/after restore leave a recoverable operation that can still be cleared.

If this tool-invocation scope and conflict-first first slice matches the intended design, please approve it and assign me; I can implement it without starting the retention or message-only-undo work.

@anomalyco Thanks for the heads up. PR #33010 and this PR take different approaches:

**PR #33010** (glibc approach): Uses `grun` (glibc-runner) to run the glibc-linked `linux-arm64` binary on Termux. Requires installing `glibc-runner` from tur-repo, and the binary still goes through glibc under the hood.

**PR #48405** (musl approach): Uses the `linux-arm64-musl` binary directly with Alpine's musl loader via patchelf. No glibc-runner needed — the binary runs natively against musl. Also fixes `isMusl()` to return true on Android so the correct package variant is selected.

The musl approach avoids the glibc dependency entirely and matches how the community has been running opencode on Termux (see [DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl](https://github.com/DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl)). Both PRs add `android:linux` to the platform map — that part is identical.

If the maintainers prefer the glibc approach, I'd close this one. But the musl approach is simpler (no extra runtime dependency) and has been tested extensively on Android 17.

The bug report is already open: #48404, created before this PR. The description includes `Closes #48404` and now also the full issue URL.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #38362: OOM crash on startup caused by large database (similar root cause — database grows too large, causing process crash on load)
- #41175: Excessive storage from event table storing full message snapshots on every streaming update (same underlying database bloat issue)
- #43551: OOM and ~30 GB database from message.updated events re-serializing full payloads (very similar root cause: unbounded database growth leading to crash)
- #47854: EventV2 cold history duplicates large snapshot payloads and amplifies SQLite storage/reads (related database bloat)

Your issue is distinct in identifying the specific WebKit `StringImpl` 2 GB string length assertion as the crash mechanism, which is a useful addition. However, the root cause (unbounded database growth) and proposed solutions (cleanup, chunked loading, retention policies) overlap significantly with the above.

Follow-up: I found the v1 → v2 regression. It is a header classification change in the Copilot provider, not the agent loop.

## v1 (dev line)

Utility traffic is explicitly classified, and titles are deliberately routed off the picker:

- `packages/opencode/src/plugin/github-copilot/copilot.ts:366` — `chat.headers` sets `X-Interaction-Type: agent-session-name-generation` when `incoming.agent === "title"`.
- `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:1974` — `getSmallModel` gives Copilot its own priority list, `["gpt-mini", ...smallModelFamilyPriority]`, and the Copilot plugin overrides the result with `UTILITY_MODELS` (`copilot.ts:355`) — models GitHub exposes for utility use but does not put in the picker.
- `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:220-230` — title generation passes `small: true`.

So in v1 a title request carried `agent-session-name-generation` and ran on a utility model.

## v2

`interactionType` in `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/github-copilot.ts:395-400` emits only four values:

```
title      -> conversation-background
compaction -> conversation-compaction
child      -> conversation-subagent
default    -> conversation-agent
```

`agent-session-name-generation` no longer appears anywhere in the v2 tree (`git grep` returns nothing), and `Catalog.model.small` uses the global `SMALL_MODEL_FAMILY_PRIORITY` (`packages/core/src/catalog.ts:226`) with no Copilot-specific branch. For a Copilot session that resolves to `gpt-5.6-luna` (family `gpt-luna`, the first entry in that list) — a normal picker model, instead of the utility model v1 used.

Net effect: a request kind that v1 sent as a free utility interaction is now sent as `conversation-background` on a picker model, so it draws from the same per-request quota as the agent loop.

## Why that is enough to drain a 1500-request plan in one session

Under the legacy plan the unit is requests, not tokens, so the model choice does not change the cost per request — what matters is how many requests leave the client. One prompt already fans out into many: one per agent-loop step, plus separate `compaction`, `title` and `generate` requests (`SessionRequestKind` in `packages/plugin/src/effect/session.ts:61`). Reclassifying the auxiliary ones from utility to metered adds them all to the same quota that the loop is already spending.

## One thing I could not pin down from the source

After the session first hits the 429, every subsequent attempt still leaves the client. `isRetryable` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/retry.ts:26`) only treats `QuotaExceeded` as non-retryable, but this error arrives as `RateLimit`, which is retryable and bounded by `Schedule.max([Schedule.exponential("2 seconds"), Schedule.recurs(4)])` — so up to ~5 attempts per step against a quota that is already exhausted. If Copilot counts those attempts, that compounds fast; if it does not count rejected requests, then the classification change above is the whole story. I have no legacy plan to test against, so I cannot tell which of the two it is.

Happy to open a PR restoring the utility classification and model routing for Copilot title requests, once we agree on the intended behaviour.

Confirming this on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, opencode 1.18.30). Same mechanism, 81 minutes pinned before I killed the holder by hand. I opened #48414 before finding this one and am closing it as a duplicate — four details from it that aren't here yet:

**There is a timeout, but it can't reach the holder.** The bash tool has a 2-minute default (10 max) and kills the process *group* with a 3s force-kill. Anything that left the group — `setsid`, and on some shells `disown` — isn't in it, so the descriptor is never released and the call is unrecoverable rather than merely slow. That may be why it looked like there was no timeout at all. An agent reaching for `setsid` to keep a job alive past the timeout converts a 2-minute stall into a permanent one.

**The holder doesn't need to produce output.** #22012 described continuously-writing processes (uvicorn, `npm run dev`), which reads as if quiet processes are fine. They aren't — the collector waits on EOF, not on data. `sleep` writes nothing and hangs it just the same:

```
sleep 3 &                                exit=5ms  stdout end=3007ms  stderr end=3009ms
sleep 3 </dev/null >/dev/null &          exit=3ms  stdout end=4ms     stderr end=3005ms
sleep 3 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &     exit=4ms  stdout end=4ms     stderr end=4ms
```

(`spawn(cmd, [], {shell:'/bin/bash', stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']})`, timing `exit` against `end` on each stream.) `exit` is immediate in all three, so PR #20901 is doing its job; the stream ends still lag by the full lifetime of the background process. Line 2 shows one un-redirected descriptor is enough.

**Redirect scope is a trap for the agent.** What hung me was:

```
setsid bash -c 'python3 -u capture.py > capture.log 2>&1' </dev/null >/dev/null &
```

That looks fully redirected, and `2>&1` is right there — but it applies to the inner python. The `bash -c` wrapper kept the tool's stderr, and `/proc/<wrapper>/fd/2` was a socket whose peer was open in the opencode process. Killing just the wrapper released the call instantly.

**Workaround, for anyone landing here:** redirect both descriptors on the backgrounded command itself (`cmd </dev/null >log 2>&1 &`), and for a job that must outlive the call use `systemd-run --user --unit=NAME --collect cmd` rather than `setsid` — it detaches without inheriting anything and survives the group kill.
